reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading files. The items it relies on all exist. history.rs has LandingIntent, Landing, LandingCommit and MergeMethod, and validate() returns BadPrNumber and BadSha("host_commit") as the criterion 6 tests expect. RecordsWriter::append creates an orphan first commit and moves the branch with a compare-and-swap update-ref. Git::rev_list_reverse is at lib.rs:457 and is_ancestor at lib.rs:352. In gh.rs, land_pr calls host.merge at line 1345 between the checks gate and the second observe_merge, and GhClient::merge picks the merge method locally at line 806, so returning it costs nothing. The hook points, the failure policy, the records paths and the demonstrations all fit the request. Each test would fail without the behavior it covers. One design gap remains. append moves the local athena/records ref before the push. sync_from, as specified, returns an error when local and remote have diverged. After a rejected push they have always diverged, so the planned "re-sync and rebuild" retry cannot work as written. Worse, an unpushed local intent left by a failed push or a crash, followed by any later write to the remote branch, makes every future land --pr fail before the merge with a divergence error. Two smaller points: Athena::land_pr is also called from drain.rs, and the post-merge state "merged but not verified" is not addressed. Findings: major: The retry after a rejected push cannot work: sync_from refuses the very divergence it must recover from, and an unpushed local commit can block every later landing. (Plan decision 9 and decision 8; crates/athena-git/src/records_branch.rs:142-150); minor: The merged-but-unverified state and the drain.rs caller are not covered. (Plan decision 2 / Files gh.rs; crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs:1347 and crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:1263); nit: Stray local commits between the base and the head would block the merge with an unclear error. (Plan decision 4)
